- Year-by-year adjusted price (high/low): 2008 H 191 / L 49.6; 2009 H 131 / L 51.2; 2010–2016 range about 76–186 (2014 low 75.95, 2016 low 83.55); 2017 close 294; 2018 close 400; 2020 close 457 (low 220 in the COVID crash); 2021 close 1,236; 2023 close 1,658; 2024 close 2,606; 2025 close 3,298 — [stockpricearchive](https://stockpricearchive.com/share-price-history-and-returns/radico/). The data has inconsistencies: the site says "no split", yet the 2005–06 figures look unadjusted.
- A 2006 stock split took face value from ₹10 to ₹2 — [Search summary citing screener/finology data](https://www.screener.in/company/RADICO/)
- Recent price about ₹4,135–4,196, 52-week range ₹2,500–4,748 — [screener.in](https://www.screener.in/company/RADICO/); [Sharekhan](https://www.sharekhan.com/stock/radico-khaitan-ltd). The sites conflict: stockpricearchive shows a 2026 YTD high of only ₹3,679 as of June 2026, so the ₹4,748 high presumably came after June 2026. Verify.
- Origin story: Radico's Shaw Wallace bottling contract expired in the mid-1990s. Lalit Khaitan approached United Spirits for a partnership and was refused, which he believed was because Vijay Mallya wanted a stake in Radico. Radico then launched its own brands. **8PM whisky launched 8 Aug 1998** — [StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/). So the real "UB" link is the 1990s Mallya rebuff, which pushed Radico to build brands of its own.
- Magic Moments vodka launched in 2005 ([HDFC Sec, Sep 2017](https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/RadicoKhaitan-PickoftheWeek-11091720170911085911.pdf)) or 2006 ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/magazine/how-radico-khaitan-is-driving-the-premiumisation-wave-in-indias-competitive-alcohol-industry)). Sources conflict. It now holds about 60% of Indian premium vodka — [StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/)
- Radico had a JV with Diageo (Diageo Radico Distilleries), which launched Masterstroke Deluxe in 2007 and was later called off — [search summary](https://www.screener.in/company/RADICO/); [Tradebrains](https://tradebrains.in/how-vijay-mallyas-united-spirits-sale-helped-diageo-dominate-indias-premium-liquor-market/)
- Diageo agreed in Nov 2012 to buy 53.4% of USL from Mallya but ended up with only 25.02% by July 2013. The open offer failed — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/diageo-seals-deal-with-mallya-to-pick-up-53-4-112110900175_1.html); [Business Standard Jul 2013](https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/diageo-gains-control-over-united-spirits-ups-stake-to-25-113070400973_1.html)
- In the early-2017 pre-rerating state, net debt was ₹742 cr and the company "has not performed well in the last two years due to increasing raw material costs" — [Angel Broking 3QFY17](https://www.angelone.in/get-html-report/AngelBrokingResearch_Radico%20Khaitan_3QFY2017RU_130217.html)
- Turnaround numbers: debt/equity fell from 0.77 (FY17) to 0.15 (FY21). Revenue rose from ₹1,680 cr to ₹2,418 cr (+44%) while PAT rose from ₹80 cr to ₹271 cr (+239%), operating leverage — [StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/)
- FY26: consolidated PAT +74.6% to ₹602.5 cr. Prestige & Above brands are now more than half of operating revenue — [search summary of FY26 analyses](https://alphastreet.com/india/radico-khaitan-premiumization-drives-strong-growth-outlook). Net debt was ₹5.7 bn at FY25 — [BS broker note](https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/market-reports/equity-brokertips/2025-06/17506722950.95489700.pdf)
- Valuepickr's long-running thread "Radico khaitan: alcoholic child" has discussion going back years — [Valuepickr](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/radico-khaitan-alcoholic-child/3062?page=4)

**Titan**
- His own account: Titan was ₹30 in October 2001, ₹61 in 2006, and later ₹600. He held because "there was no permanent impairment of value." — [Outlook Business interview](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/you-cant-make-money-on-borrowed-knowledge-566)
- He bought 664,250 shares between March and June 2002, around ₹50 unadjusted. — [Open Magazine](https://openthemagazine.com/features/living/jhunjhunwalas-real-bull-run). He and Rekha held 1.57% by June 2002, worth ₹5.2 crore unadjusted (₹26 lakh adjusted). — [Fortune India 2018](https://fortuneindia-web.quintype.io/investing/rakesh-jhunjhunwalas-titanic-journey/India's richest)
- The "₹3" figure is a split- and bonus-adjusted price: Titan was ₹3.26 adjusted on 5 September 2002. — per [Business Today/Atul Suri](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/top-story/story/80000-return-in-20-years-atul-suri-explains-how-mentor-rakesh-jhunjunwala-spotted-titan-stock-346458-2022-09-06). Other blogs cite ₹5 or ₹30, which mixes adjusted and unadjusted prices.
- In 2018 they held 8.46%, then sold about 1.25 crore shares for about ₹1,093 crore, leaving 7.37% (about ₹5,480 crore). — [Fortune India](https://fortuneindia-web.quintype.io/investing/rakesh-jhunjhunwalas-titanic-journey/India's richest)
- At death (June 2022 quarter): a 5.10% stake worth ₹11,086.9 crore, his largest holding and about one-third of a 32-stock portfolio. — [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239); [ThePrint profile](https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/rakesh-jhunjhunwala-was-investor-with-midas-touch-who-never-gave-up-on-indian-markets/1654819). Bloomberg says more than a third including Rekha's holdings, with stock holdings of nearly $4bn. — [BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/indian-billionaire-s-stock-holdings-worth-nearly-4-billion-in-focus-after-death-1.1806140.amp.html)
- His disclosed portfolio rose from ₹8,431 crore in March 2020 to ₹30,652 crore in August 2022. Forbes net worth at death was $5.8bn. — [Business Standard (via search)](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/rakesh-jhunjhunwala-s-near-4-bn-stock-holdings-in-focus-after-death-122081600674_1.html); [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/rakesh-jhunjhunwala-was-investor-with-midas-touch-who-never-gave-up-on-indian-markets/1654819)

`case_study:theranos-2015` | 2015-10-15 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Private blood-testing startup Theranos was valued at ~$9 bn (2014) on claims that a finger-prick device could run hundreds of tests. In Oct 2015 John Carreyrou (WSJ) revealed it ran most tests on modified commercial analysers and that its own device was unreliable; regulators sanctioned its lab; the company dissolved in 2018. Elizabeth Holmes was convicted on four fraud counts and sentenced to 11.25 years (Nov 2022). Visible flags: (1) no peer-reviewed data or independent validation; (2) a board of statesmen/generals rather than lab scientists; (3) extreme secrecy and NDAs, employee turnover; (4) investors (family offices, media owners) without healthcare diligence; Walgreens' partnership skipped proper testing; (5) founder charisma substituted for evidence. Lesson for listed markets: deep-tech/biotech claims need third-party validation (peer review, regulatory approvals, customer audits); a 'celebrity' board is a governance red flag, not comfort. Included briefly as a private-market case; no listed tickers.

**Lesson:** Demand independent validation of technical claims
**Spotted early by:** John Carreyrou (WSJ); whistleblowers Tyler Shultz, Erika Cheung
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`
**Sources:** <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-11-18/holmes-sentence-over-theranos-may-set-silicon-valley-example> ; <https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/elizabeth-holmes-sentenced-theranos-trial-rcna57344>

`strategy:marks-cycle-temperature` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: global, india, process, base-rate, avoid-ruin

You can't predict, but you can prepare: estimate where the market is in its cycle and adjust aggression gradually. Marks's 'temperature' inputs: investor psychology (greed vs fear), credit availability and lending standards, issuance quality (IPOs of loss-making or tiny firms), valuation vs history, and the prevailing narrative ('this time is different'). Indian temperature checklist: smallcap/midcap P/E premium to Nifty; mainboard and SME IPO counts and subscription multiples; retail F&O volumes and new demat additions; market cap/GDP (above ~120% = hot, below ~70% = cold, per 2008/2020/2024 history); NBFC/corporate bond spreads; FPI positioning and the rupee. Posture rule: in hot readings, raise quality, trim small caps, keep dry powder; in cold readings, deploy in steps. Second-level thinking: ask what consensus expects and what is priced, not just whether a company is good. Limitation: temperature readings are early by months or years.

Links: person:howard-marks (about); insight:india-cycle-top-bottom-signals (about)

Sources: <https://www.privatedebtinvestor.com/oaktree-raises-10-9bn-distressed-fund/>
